https://www.walesonline.co.uk/lifestyle/.text: Channel 4 's Taskmaster is returning for a new series in a matter of weeks and the confirmation comes after Greg Davies admitted how his co-host "genuinely annoys" him. Welshman Greg, who is from St Asaph, will return to Channel 4 alongside Alex Horne on Thursday, September 3 for series 22. But recently, the 58-year-old stand-up comedian admitted there are things his co-host does that "genuinely annoys" him. Greg told Metro: "I think he deliberately sits down and thinks: 'I know how to get Greg into character, and it's to properly wind him up.' He says things that have no structure, punchline [or] comic premise, and it genuinely annoys me. "[The scoring] is my revenge. It's the little things he doesn't like. When I give two contestants the same score, if you look into his eyes, his little brain is on fire with rage because he wants things put into boxes." But hopefully there won't be too much squabbling between them when the series returns with a number of famous names among the cast including Peep Show's Isy Suttie, Doctor Who's Matt Lucas, ventriloquist comedian Nina Conti, stand-up comedian Chloe Petts and The Bad Guys' Richard Ayoade. The tasks this time around will see the celebs "crawl through secret tunnels, look for faces on toast, go on holiday with shoes and make interesting use of their armpits", reports Digital Spy. In an interview with Polygon in June, Greg said their "roles have become organically defined, rather than in those first few seasons — sorry, series — when we sat down and decided what the dynamics should be and how we should respond". He added: "They were almost 'eggy' in comparison to where we are now, which is that we both know the limits of our roles and what the dynamic is. It feels a lot more fun now, to be honest, because we know the [Taskmaster] world and the limitations to the world." Taskmaster has been expanding across the globe in recent years, with the YouTube channel almost doubling its views across 2025. Earlier this year, it was announced that a Polish version is on the way, which is the 14th international version. The upcoming season of Taskmaster UK will return to the UK on Thursday, September 3 at 9pm - its usual time slot - and will then drop an hour later on the Taskmaster YouTube channel around the world. Taskmaster returns to Channel 4 on September 3

https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-insti.text: BRUSSELS — The European Union institutions kept calm and carried on regulating on Friday, as many other parts of the world muttered at their computers over a massive digital outage at U.S. tech leader Microsoft. The European Commission, Council of the EU and European Parliament were able to carry on business as usual, with systems remaining largely unaffected. Microsoft’s global outage , which disrupted Outlook, Teams and Copilot started on Thursday, with internet traffic monitoring site Downdetector reporting issues in at least 74 countries. The tracker logged nearly 140,000 reports of Outlook problems at its peak. Advertisement Advertisement Microsoft on Friday morning said recovery was still uneven . "At this time, we have no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident. We will continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation," it said. At the European Commission “the impact ... is very limited and does not affect our operations,” spokesperson Thomas Regnier told POLITICO. He said the outage had a “minor impact on a limited number of applications, such as the slowness of SharePoint.” Outlook and Teams were “fully operational,” Regnier said. The Council of the EU, which gathers representatives of national governments, also carried on work: Outlook and Teams were “working on our side,” a Council official told POLITICO, declining to give more details on the institution’s IT setup. The Parliament's press service said in a statement to POLITICO that it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation as a precaution. The outage is exposing the reliance of companies and governments on Microsoft services — an issue that has also been a longstanding concern in Europe among proponents of keeping more control over IT and digital infrastructure. In October last year, a similar outage of Amazon Web Services servers prompted immediate calls for Europe to boost its tech sovereignty . Advertisement Advertisement Efforts to move away from American tech providers got a boost in the past two years due to concerns that the U.S. administration of Donald Trump could disrupt digital services in Europe for political gain. Governments across Europe have launched a wide range of initiatives to boost local competitors to U.S. Big Tech and build public services on homegrown platforms. One example is the government of Germany’s northernmost state of Schleswig-Holstein, which in 2025 moved about 40,000 mailboxes from Microsoft Exchange and Outlook to open-source alternatives to reduce their reliance on U.S. tech. The state's digitalization minister, Dirk Schrödter, said in a comment to POLITICO on Friday that disruptions like the Microsoft outage “must be taken very seriously,” whether the state uses open-source software or products from individual providers. “We must be able to intervene ourselves at any time if problems arise,” he said. Francesca Micheletti contributed to this report.
